insider_note: A linear factor MULTIPLYING a square root, rather than divided by one, is the signal for this A·f′(x)·√f(x)+B·√f(x) split — the A-part becomes a clean power of f(x) with no log or inverse function at all.

steps.label: Write the multiplier as A·Dr′ + B and solve for A, B
steps.why: Writing the outside multiplier as A times the derivative of the expression under the root (plus a leftover B) is the same idea used earlier in this chapter, now for a MULTIPLIED root instead of a divided one.
common_mistakes: Confusing this with the A·Dr′+B split used for a root in the DENOMINATOR and expecting the same final formula.
Sign slip: −A+B=−2 with A=3/4 gives B=−2+3/4=−5/4, not −2−3/4.
steps.memory_tip: −(3/4)+B=−2 ⇒ B=−2+3/4 — adding 3/4, not subtracting it, when moving −A to the other side.

steps.label: Substitute back and split the integral
steps.why: ∫f′(x)√f(x) dx is a plain power-rule integral in disguise (u=f(x), du=f′(x)dx gives ∫√u du = (2/3)u^{3/2}) — no completing the square is needed for THIS half of the answer.
common_mistakes: Trying to complete the square before splitting off the A-part, which is unnecessary extra work.
Missing the exponent 3/2, writing a plain square instead.
steps.memory_tip: ∫f′√f dx = (2/3)f^{3/2} — the SAME shape as ∫f′/√f dx = 2√f, one power higher.

steps.label: Complete the square and apply the standard √(x²+a²) form
steps.why: The leftover B∫√f(x) dx piece genuinely needs completing the square, since here the root cannot be reduced by a simple substitution — it needs the standard √(u²+a²) result.
common_mistakes: Applying the standard formula to the WHOLE √(2x²−x+1) directly, forgetting the √2 factored out in front.
Sign or fraction slip completing (x−1/4)²+7/16 from 2x²−x+1.
steps.memory_tip: Factor out the leading 2 from under the root FIRST — the standard formula only accepts a bare u²+a² inside.

steps.label: Combine for the final answer
steps.why: Multiplying B=−5/4 into the √2 factored out and the standard formula's own two terms gives the second and third parts of the final answer, both written with (4x−1) in place of 4(x−1/4).
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply B=−5/4 through BOTH terms of the standard √(u²+a²) result, not just one of them.
Losing the √2 that was factored outside the root back in step 3.
steps.memory_tip: B multiplies BOTH halves of the two-term standard result — the u√(u²+a²) piece and the sinh⁻¹ piece — never just one.
